title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-21
lineage: CD -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> Samplitude Professional v9.12 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: A pristine Charlie Miller‑fixed soundboard captures a late‑1973 powerhouse show highlighted by the legendary Mississippi Half‑Step → Playing in the Band → El Paso → Wharf Rat → Morning Dew sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean, well‑spliced SBD that lets every nuance of the band shine, and the performance itself ranks among the top shows of ’73.  Highlights include an inspired Here Comes Sunshine, a soaring Jack Straw, and the epic second‑set jam marathon that threads Half‑Step through Playing in the Band, El Paso, Wharf Rat and Morning Dew.  While a few listeners note missing track labels and one odd “awkward” Me & My Uncle opener, the consensus is overwhelmingly positive.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈20/25) award 5‑star ratings and praise both the musical performance and the Miller‑fixed soundboard; only a handful of minor complaints exist, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s fix provides crystal‑clear mix with expertly spliced audience patches; reviewers call it a “5‑star transfer”. Minor gripe about lack of track/label metadata, but no audible defects.

standout_songs: Playing in the Band (the long sequence)
poor_songs: Me & My Uncle (mentioned as an awkward opener)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is strong and vocal‑rich, but the second set steals the show with a seamless, jazzy jam marathon that builds momentum from Half‑Step through to Morning Dew and finishes with a high‑energy Truckin’/One More Saturday Night encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for flawless tone (beardless), soaring solos on Jack Straw, Big River, and the extended jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for “bottom‑end melodies” weaving with Garcia’s lead, especially on Here Comes Sunshine and the second‑set jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned indirectly – a reviewer suggests focusing on Jerry and Bill first, then letting Weir “sneak up”, implying solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is repeatedly lauded for rhythmic creativity, jazzy comping, and “toy[ing] around” during the band jams; several reviewers call this period his best.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann receives specific shout‑outs (e.g., “focus on Jerry and Bill”), indicating strong drumming throughout.
